Christianity: discouraged but accepted (Anglican remarriage allowed); Islam: triple talaq (Sunni); Catholicism only annulment.

walkthroughs.body_html:
If God is all-powerful and all-loving, why is there evil?

Moral evil (human-caused) and natural evil (earthquakes, disease) both demand a reply.

Epicurus framed the challenge: God is unable, unwilling, or doesn't exist.

Augustinian theodicy (Augustine, 354-430): evil came from the misuse of human free will (the Fall). Evil is the absence of good (privatio boni), not a thing.

Irenaean theodicy (Irenaeus, 2nd c.; updated by John Hick): God made us imperfect on purpose. Suffering helps us grow toward God — 'soul-making'.

Free-will defence: real love requires choice; choice means evil is possible.

Medical ethics: abortion (sanctity of life vs woman's autonomy), euthanasia (mercy vs only God decides), IVF (gift of life vs creating spare embryos).

Sexual ethics: marriage, cohabitation, same-sex relationships — natural law gives traditional answers, situation ethics is more flexible.

Environment: stewardship — humans care for creation (Genesis 1:28). Islam: humans are khalifah (trustees). Climate change is a religious issue for both.
